title: Q-LOOP-IMPROVE: every loop scores itself each tick and the worst loop gets one change per week (strange loop)
body:
**Owner:** executor
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** grep:foundation/loops.py::LOOP-IMPROVE-1
**Status:** closed

Owner directive 2026-11-12: the system always completes all work automatically and closes, resolves or archives every session and thread when complete, with no zombie idle sessions; loops do not only close, each loop gets better.

Build LOOP-IMPROVE-1 in foundation/loops.py. For every row of instances/ultrastable/loop-registry.json compute from existing logs (ops/executor-log.jsonl, ops/fleet-log.jsonl, GitHub run history) a score per tick: closed-without-human share, time from trigger to closing probe, failure rate. Write the scores to ops/loop-scores.jsonl. Each week the lowest-scoring loop gets one queued improvement item (Q-IMPROVE-<loop>-<date>) with a prediction in the form metric op number within N h; the next week's score decides keep or revert. The improvement loop is itself a registry row and is scored by the same code, so the measure improves the measurer.

Also: completion sweep (scripts/completion_sweep.sh) must report zombie sessions and unmerged branches as a metric (zombie_sessions, target 0) and fail the daily lane run when it is above 0 for two ticks.

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-21T18:12:26Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 219.0 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
